title: Batch markdown report does not escape dynamic table cells

evidence.quote:
for item in report["items"]:
        if item["status"] == "success":
            lines.append(
                "| success "
                f"| {item['video_id']} "
                f"| {_batch_text(item.get('date'))} "
                f"| {_batch_text(item.get('city'))} "
                f"| {_batch_text(_item_auction_name(item))} "
                f"| {_batch_text(_item_auctioneer(item))} "
                f"| {item['total_lots']} "
                f"| {item['total_animals']} "
                f"| {item['avg_price']:.2f} |"
            )
        else:
            lines.append(f"| failed | {item['url']} | - | - | - | - | 0 | 0 | 0.00 |")

reasoning: Batch markdown cells are populated from extracted metadata, failed URLs, and category names. Those values can contain Markdown table metacharacters such as `|` or newlines, and the formatter interpolates them directly, producing malformed `comparison.md` tables with extra columns or broken rows.
reproduction: Build a batch report with `city='Campo Grande | MS'` or a category named `bezerro | nelore`, then call `_format_batch_markdown(report)`; the rendered table row/header no longer has the intended column count.
recommendation: Add a small Markdown table-cell escaping helper and apply it to every dynamic table cell and header value before joining rows, including failed URLs and price category names.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked batch tests assert happy-path markdown strings with ordinary metadata and category names, but they do not include pipes, newlines, or other table-breaking characters.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a batch report test with metadata and category names containing `|` and newlines, then assert the rendered markdown escapes pipes and keeps stable table columns.
minimumFixScope: `main.py` batch markdown formatting helpers plus focused `tests/test_batch.py` coverage.
